paper.title: Batched Stochastic Linear Bandits with 1-Bit Communication Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Batched stochastic linear bandits with 1-bit communication constraints (finite-variance noise)
unmapped: Horizon split into fixed-size batches of size B (batch size B is fixed, not a free number of batches); the learner pre-commits B arm pulls per batch

The learner never sees rewards: per batch the agent returns a single bit Q_m(Y_batch), where Q_m is a learner-chosen 1-bit quantization function depending only on past bits (batch-wise memoryless agent)
Noise is i.i.d., zero-mean with variance at most sigma^2 (known), only finite variance assumed

settings.name_in_paper: Batched linear bandits with 1-bit feedback per batch (lower bound, holds even noiseless)
unmapped: Fixed batch size B with one bit of learner-specified quantized feedback per batch; learner does not observe rewards
Lower bound holds for any noise variance sigma^2 >= 0, including the noiseless case

algorithms.name: 1-Bit Phased Elimination with Uniform Arm Allocations (Algorithm 1)
1-bit Phased Elimination with Safe Arm and Warm Start (Algorithm 2)

symbols.B_batch: batch size (number of pulls per batch, one bit of feedback per batch)

conditions: exists an action set of size K with max ||a||_2 <= 1

source.label: thm:minimax_lower
source.quote: For any dimension $d \ge 1$, horizon $T \ge 1$, batch size $B \ge 1$, reward noise variance $\sigma^2 \ge 0$, and integer $K \ge 16$, there exists an action set $\cA$ of size $\lvert \cA \rvert = K$ with $\max_{a \in \cA} \|a\|_2 \le 1$ such that for every algorithm operating in $M=\lceil T/B\rceil$ batches that receives only one bit of feedback per batch, the expected cumulative regret satisfies $\sup_{\|\theta\|_2 \le 1} \mathbb{E}[R_T] = \Omega(\min\{T, B\min(d,\log \lvert \cA \rvert)\})$.

results.notes: Regret defined via means <a*-A_t, theta>, so E[R_T] is pseudo-regret. Holds in the noiseless case, hence recorded with noise_free.

conditions: exists an action set of the given size with max ||a||_2 <= 1

source.label: cor:general_lower_bound
source.quote: Under the setup in Theorem~\ref{thm:minimax_lower} with $\sigma = \Theta(1)$, for any specified set size $\lvert\cA\rvert$, there exists a corresponding action set $\cA$ of that size with $\max_{a\in\cA}\|a\|_2 \le 1$ such that the expected cumulative regret satisfies $\sup_{\|\theta\|_2\le 1}\mathbb{E}[R_T] = \widetilde{\Omega}(\min\{T, B\min\{d,\log\lvert\cA\rvert\} + \sqrt{dT\min\{d,\log\lvert\cA\rvert\}}\})$.

results.notes: Combines Theorem 1 with lower bounds of Zhou et al. 2019 for standard linear bandits. Simplifies to min{T, dB + d sqrt(T)} when |A| = exp(Omega(d)) and min{T, B log|A| + sqrt(dT log|A|)} when |A| = exp(O(d)). Exact noise distribution of the hard instance not specified by the corollary.

conditions: every non-mixing algorithm (a single arm pulled B times in each batch)
action set is the standard basis {e_1,...,e_d} (K = d)

source.label: thm:non_mixing_lb
source.quote: Fix a dimension $d \ge 2$, horizon $T \ge 1$, batch size $B \ge 1$, and reward noise variance $\sigma^2 \ge 0$. Let the action set be the standard basis $\cA = \{e_1,\dots,e_d\}$. For every non-mixing algorithm (as defined above), we have $\sup_{\theta\in \mathcal{A}} \mathbb{E}[R_T] = \Omega(\min\{T, dB\})$.

results.notes: Proof even allows unquantized feedback; restricted to non-mixing algorithms.

tuning: confidence parameter delta in (0,1) given to the algorithm

source.label: thm:exp_A_upper
source.quote: Fix a finite action set $\cA \subset \bR^d$, and consider the problem described in Section \ref{sec:problem_setup} with time horizon $T \in \bN$, variance $\sigma^2 = \Theta(1)$, and batch size $B \in \{1,\dots, T\}$. Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, there exists an algorithm ... that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, incurs a regret of at most $R_T = \widetilde{O}( dB\log(\frac{1}{\delta}) + d\sqrt{T\log(\frac{1}{\delta})})$, where $\widetilde{O}$ hides logarithmic dependencies on $d$ and $T$.

results.notes: Independent of |A|; Remark 2 extends it to infinite compact sets via covering with O(1) extra regret. With delta = 1/T gives expected regret matching lower bound when |A| = exp(Omega(d)).

tuning: confidence parameter delta in (0,1) given to the algorithm

source.label: thm:poly_A_upper
source.quote: Fix a finite action set $\cA \subset \bR^d$. For the problem described in Section \ref{sec:problem_setup} with time horizon $T \in \bN$, variance $\sigma^2 = \Theta(1)$, and batch size $B \in \{1,\dots, T\}$, there exists an algorithm ... that, with probability at least $1-\delta$, incurs a regret of at most $R_T = \widetilde{O}(B \log ( \frac{\lvert \cA \rvert }{\delta}) + d^{\frac{3}{2}}\sqrt{B} \log^{\frac{5}{2}}(\frac{\lvert \cA \rvert}{\delta}) + \sqrt{dT \log (\frac{\lvert \cA \rvert}{\delta})})$, where $\widetilde{O}$ hides logarithmic dependencies on $d$ and $T$.

results.notes: Footnote: first two terms can be tightened to min with dB log(|A|/delta). Computation polynomial in |A| and d.

conditions: holds on the good event E_3, which has probability at least 1 - delta/3
tuning: Algorithm 2 run without safe-arm / warm-start pre-processing (A_1 = A)

source.label: thm:step3_small_b_regret
source.quote: Under $\cE_3$, the cumulative regret incurred by the standalone phased elimination algorithm (i.e., Algorithm \ref{alg:poly_action_set} without warm start) satisfies $R_{T} = \widetilde{O}( dB\log(\frac{\lvert\cA\rvert}{\delta}) + \sqrt{dT\log(\frac{\lvert\cA\rvert}{\delta})})$.

results.notes: Stated conditional on event E_3 (Lemma 20: P(E_3) >= 1-delta/3). Algorithm is Step 3 of Algorithm 2 standalone.

source.label: cor:poly_A_upper
source.quote: When $\lvert \cA \rvert = {\rm poly}(d)$ and $\sigma = \Theta(1)$, the expected regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:poly_action_set} is bounded by $\mathbb{E}[R_T] = \widetilde{O}\left(B + d^{\frac{3}{2}}\sqrt{B} + \sqrt{dT} \right)$.

results.notes: Corollary 7 further states this is minimax optimal up to polylog when B = Omega(d^3) or T = Omega(d^2 B), and within O_tilde(sqrt(d)) of the lower bound otherwise (ratio statement, not recorded separately).
